title: 2009 AMC 12B Problem 7
statement: In a certain year the price of gasoline rose by \(20\%\) during January, fell by \(20\%\) during February, rose by \(25\%\) during March, and fell by \(x\%\) during April. The price of gasoline at the end of April was the same as it had been at the beginning of January. To the nearest integer, what is \(x?\)

solutions.text:
After January through March the price is \(1.2 \cdot 0.8 \cdot 1.25 = 1.2\) times the original.

To return to the original, April must multiply by \(\dfrac{1}{1.2},\) a decrease of \(1 - \dfrac{1}{1.2} = \dfrac{1}{6} \approx 16.7\%.\) To the nearest integer, \(x = 17.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: After three months the price is \(1.2\) times the start, so April must undo that factor
